correctness.rationale: A fort has a nonempty spine support S and contains the mates of selected spine vertices. At an unselected spine vertex the leaf is forbidden, required, or optional when it has respectively 0, 1, or 2 selected spine neighbors. Remove all optional leaves to obtain the canonical F(S). For nonempty T⊆S, canonical inclusion F(T)⊆F(S) fails exactly when T separates the two neighbors of an unselected spine vertex that had two selected neighbors in S. This is precisely a cut of an edge in the frozen distance-two link graph. Hence F(S) is minimal iff that graph is connected. The frozen proof's suggestion that every proper fort of a canonical fort is itself canonical is unnecessary and need not hold; every such fort contains its own canonical subfort, which is all the inclusion test needs. Connected supports are exactly step-two intervals; the adjacent boundary leaves are the only extra vertices. With k selected spine vertices there are n−2k+2 starts, two touching one endpoint except when both endpoints are touched by the unique longest progression at odd n. This yields the stated polynomial, count, extrema, and the single-edge case n=1. The inspected verify.py uses the defining neighborhood test plus a proper-subset dynamic program, matching the recorded full-family comparisons through n=9; it does not prove the infinite result. No uploaded code was run.

evidence: Cameron–Li Theorem 3.3 gives an iff criterion for every tree: at most one inside neighbor at an included vertex, zero or two inside neighbors at an excluded vertex, and no edge with both endpoints excluded can separate the fort.

Abiad–Ghasemi Nezhad provide a linear-time, linear-space scalar count algorithm for any tree; Dat–Kenter provide general upper bounds and finite maxima. Neither latter item alone gives the frozen symbolic profile.
Resultary 866a6a844b58 gives a broader link-graph theorem for every whiskered tree; its date key is later than the frozen record.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The cut characterization, rather than an algorithm or extremal bound, is the prior theorem strong enough to force the exact structure without a new comb-specific minimality argument.

evidence: Condition (b) forces the mate of every selected spine vertex to be selected and rules out a nonempty fort of leaves alone. For each excluded spine vertex, (b) fixes its leaf to be selected exactly when there is one selected spine neighbor. Condition (a) now forbids adjacent selected spine vertices.

If consecutive selected spine indices differed by at least three, the intermediate edge between two consecutive excluded spine vertices would separate the fort, violating (c). Thus consecutive selected indices differ exactly by two. Conversely the resulting sets satisfy (a) and (b); no spine edge with both ends outside separates the fort, and deleting a pendant edge with both ends outside only isolates an excluded leaf, so (c) holds.

As soon as the two endpoints are known the boundary indicators fix the size. Counting the possible starts gives the polynomial and quadratic count, and the length-one spine gives its unique two-vertex fort.
